intended_object: The set G(K) of K-rational points of a K-scheme f : G → Spec K, i.e. the sections Spec K → G of f. When G is a group scheme over K this set is a group. Inferred from the docstring and from how the component-group file uses it.
explanation:
In the category Over (Spec K), the monoidal unit 𝟙_ of the cartesian monoidal structure is the terminal object, which is (Spec K, 𝟙). So a morphism 𝟙_ ⟶ Over.mk f is a morphism s : Spec K → G with s ≫ f = 𝟙, that is, a section of f. That is exactly a K-rational point. Defining it as a hom-set out of the unit is a good choice: Mathlib's GrpObj instances then give it its group structure automatically when Over.mk f is a group object, as the docstring says.

On generality: the same construction would give S-points of an S-scheme over any base S. But the name and docstring are specifically about K-rational points, and the rest of the file needs the field. It evaluates points at `IsLocalRing.closedPoint K` and relies on Spec K being a one-point space. Mathlib has no named definition of rational points or sections of a structure morphism that this duplicates; it only has the generic hom-set out of the unit, which this abbrev specializes. So it is not too narrow, and it is faithful.
